seo_title: 12 Questions to Ask Your Wedding Photographer | Zen Visuals
seo_description: The twelve questions worth asking a wedding photographer before you book, and the answers you want to hear, from Derbyshire wedding photographers Zen Visuals.
h1: Twelve questions to ask your wedding photographer
hero_alt: Groom with six bridesmaids in rust and sage dresses
intro: You'll spend more of your wedding day with your photographer than with most of your guests. These are the questions that tell you whether they're the right one, and the answers we'd want to hear.
We're Zuzia and Ben of Zen Visuals, wedding photographers and videographers in Belper, Derbyshire.

sections.heading: 1. Can we see a full wedding gallery?
sections.text: Not a portfolio: a whole day, start to finish, from a wedding like yours. You're looking for consistency through bad light, dark venues and the evening.

sections.heading: 2. Who will photograph our wedding?
sections.text: The answer should be a name, and ideally the person you're talking to.

sections.heading: 3. How long will you be there?
sections.text: Ask whether coverage is by the hour or for the day, and what happens if the day runs late. Ours covers the whole day, with no clock.

sections.heading: 4. How many photographs will we get, and how are they edited?
sections.text: A full day usually produces several hundred finished photographs. Ask whether every one is edited, and whether the style you see online is what you'll receive.

sections.heading: 5. How long until we see them?
sections.text: Three to six weeks is a fair answer. Ask whether you'll get a preview sooner.

sections.heading: 6. How do you handle group photographs?
sections.text: A good photographer has a short list agreed in advance and gets through it in twenty minutes, so you can get back to your guests.

sections.heading: 7. What do you do if it rains?
sections.text: Listen for a real plan: indoor light they like at your venue, umbrellas, a short window outside if the weather breaks.

sections.heading: 8. Have you worked at our venue?
sections.text: Useful but not essential. A good photographer who hasn't will visit or arrive early.

sections.heading: 9. How do you work alongside a videographer?
sections.text: If you're having both, you want people who plan together. Booking photography and film from one team removes the problem.

sections.heading: 10. What's in the price, and what's extra?
sections.text: Travel, a second photographer, an engagement shoot, albums, prints. Get the list in writing.

sections.heading: 11. What happens if you're ill?
sections.text: They should have a network of photographers they trust and a plan for cover.

sections.heading: 12. How do we book, and when is the balance due?
sections.text: Expect a contract, a deposit to secure the date and a clear date for the balance. Ours is half to book and the rest any time up to two weeks after the wedding.

faqs.question: How much does a wedding photographer cost in the UK?
faqs.answer: Whole-day wedding photography in the UK commonly runs from around £800 to £2,500 and up. Ours is £1,000 for the whole day in Derbyshire.

faqs.question: How many hours should a wedding photographer stay?
faqs.answer: Long enough to cover getting ready through to the first dance and some of the party, usually ten to twelve hours. Whole-day pricing avoids the problem.

faqs.question: Should we book photography and film from the same company?
faqs.answer: If you want both, one team that works together means fewer people in the room, no fighting for the same angle, and a consistent style across your photographs and film.
